summary: Gauri Viswanathan is an Indologist who studied at the University of Delhi (~1968–1973) and Columbia University (~1978–1985). She lectured in English at Delhi, held fellowships at IISH (1998) and Princeton (2000), and became Class of 1933 Professor at Columbia (~1989).

Gavin D'Costa works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Cambridge and at the University of Birmingham under John Hick (~1981–1985). He taught at West London Institute (~1985–1990) and became Emeritus Professor of Catholic Theology at Bristol (1993).

Gavin Flood specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith (~1983–1989). He held professorships at Oxford (2005–2015), Stirling (~2005–2008), and Yale-NUS College (2016), directing the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (2005–2015).
Geetha K. Wilson is an Indologist who has been a doctoral student under Claire Maes and a faculty member at the University of Tübingen (attested 2026).

Gelek is a scholar of Tibetology. He has worked as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998) and served as a visiting lecturer at the University of California and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

Gelek Rimpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell University under teachers including Ling and Trijang Rinpoches. He served as director of Tibet House, New Delhi (1965), and founded Jewel Heart (1988).

Gembo Dorji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Jigme Choedra. He completed his education at Tango Buddhist Institute, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indologist and historian who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, at the University of Tokyo. He worked as a researcher at CEACS (~1962–1967) and Toyo Bunko (~1965–1974), later becoming a professor at Kokugakuin University (2006).

Genchi Kato worked in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue. He taught at the Imperial Japanese Army (1906–1933) and the University of Tokyo (1920–1933), later becoming a professor at Kokugakuin and Taisho universities (1933).
Gendun Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He founded several centres, including Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, where he served as abbot and retreat master from around 1977 to 1997.

Gendün Chöphel was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Drisha, Kumbum, Labrang, and Drepung monasteries under Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso, and he was affiliated with the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

Geng Shimin was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China (~1952–1953) and subsequently held a post there from around 1953 to 2000.

Genjun Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who graduated from Kyoto University and studied under scholars such as Susumu Yamaguchi and Johannes Nobel. He was a professor at Otani University and served as a Fulbright professor at Harvard.
Genro was an 18th-century Buddhist figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the senior monastic rank of daiichiza at Myoshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his studies at Komazawa University (~1930–1934) and later served as a professor there from around 1960 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral degrees at Waseda University. He was an assistant professor at Kokushikan University (~1958–1964) and professor emeritus at Rissho University (1980–1996).
Genshu Watanabe was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Toyo University and became the dharma heir of Daiun Sogaku Harada.
Genzao was a practitioner and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche, and trained at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950.

Geo Widengren was a scholar of Iranian-Central Asian and religious studies. He studied at Stockholm University and Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, serving as professor of the history of religions at Uppsala (1940–1973) and president of the IAHR (~1960–1970).

Geoff Childs is an anthropologist of Tibet and historian who earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under Tsetan Chonjore. He was an Andrew Mellon Postdoctoral Fellow at ANU and taught anthropology at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 2003–2005).
